source_name: Erste Bank Hungary Zrt. – Éves jelentések
why_relevant: Erste HU is a top-5 issuer and a significant POS acquirer; its annual report and management report carry card counts, network size and acquiring commentary. Reports published in HU and EN.

source_name: Erste Bank Hungary – hivatalos közzétételek (regulatory announcements)
why_relevant: Announcement stream that points to each newly published financial/Pillar 3 document; the cheapest way to detect when new Erste HU disclosure drops.

source_name: K&H Bank Zrt. – éves, féléves és negyedéves jelentések
why_relevant: K&H (KBC group) is a top-5 HU issuer/acquirer. The page hosts individual and consolidated annual reports in HU and EN PDF, containing card and channel volume disclosures.

source_name: KBC Group Investor Relations – Hungary business unit reporting
why_relevant: K&H is unlisted in Hungary, so segment-level Hungarian KPIs (digital sales share, mobile app users, customer counts) appear in KBC Group's quarterly reports and 'digital-first' KPI slides rather than in K&H's own filings.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. – Tőkepiaci törvény szerinti jelentések
why_relevant: Raiffeisen HU publishes consolidated business reports (konszolidált üzleti jelentés) under capital-markets law because of its bond issuance; these contain retail/card business commentary and network data for a top-6 issuer.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Hungary / UniCredit Jelzálogbank – éves és gyorsjelentések
why_relevant: UniCredit's Hungarian disclosure route; the mortgage-bank IR pages point to group-level Hungarian filings including ESEF/xhtml annual reports carrying business and network data for a top-8 issuer/acquirer.

source_name: CIB Bank Zrt. – Annual reports / jelentések
why_relevant: CIB (Intesa Sanpaolo) annual and consolidated reports; consolidated statements observed via BÉT mirror with 2024 totals, and the business report sections cover retail cards and channel network.

source_name: GRÁNIT Bank Nyrt. – Befektetőknek (investor relations)
why_relevant: Gránit is the HU digital-native bank and now BÉT-listed, so it discloses digital KPIs other banks keep private: digital account opening, cardless digital card issuance, retail/corporate account counts (e.g. 13,924 corporate accounts reported), and growth of digital channels. The best proxy for HU digital-payments adoption from the issuer side.

source_name: BÉT / Budapest Stock Exchange – kibinfo issuer disclosure archive (newkibdata)
why_relevant: Central mirror where OTP, Gránit, Raiffeisen, Erste HU and CIB actually file their annual reports, Pillar 3 and half-year reports as durable PDFs. Often more reliable and more crawlable than each bank's own CMS, and it timestamps publication.

source_name: MNB tőkepiaci közzétételek portál (kozzetetelek.mnb.hu)
why_relevant: Statutory disclosure platform operated by the central bank where HU issuers and capital-market institutions file. Catches disclosures from banks that are not BÉT-listed (Erste HU, CIB, UniCredit, K&H bond programmes) and provides stable downloadkozzetetel document IDs.

source_name: Elektronikus Beszámoló Portál – beszámoló kereső (e-beszamolo.im.gov.hu)
why_relevant: Ministry of Justice repository of every Hungarian company's filed annual accounts including the üzleti jelentés narrative. This is the fallback route to the statutory reports of banks with weak or paywalled IR pages (CIB, UniCredit HU, K&H) and to card-scheme/acquirer subsidiaries.

source_name: Magyar Bankszövetség (Hungarian Banking Association) – jelentések
why_relevant: Industry body that aggregates and comments on member banks' figures; its reports and Gazdaság és Pénzügy journal provide sector-level card/ATM/branch context and often name the banks behind trends — a bridge between individual bank disclosure and market totals.

source_name: OPTEN céginfó company profiles for HU banks
why_relevant: Commercial company-intelligence vendor with structured financial history per bank entity (K&H, Raiffeisen, UniCredit observed). Useful for normalising entity identifiers and for time-series financials when statutory PDFs are inconsistent.

source_name: Portfolio.hu banking coverage of HU bank results
why_relevant: Leading HU financial media; reports bank results and often extracts the card/digital KPIs buried in decks, and covers unlisted banks whose own disclosure is thin. Acts as a discovery layer pointing to primary documents.

source_name: MBH Befektetési Bank – equity research notes on HU listed banks
why_relevant: Sell-side research desk publishing free PDF notes on HU banks (a 2024 Gránit annual-results note observed). Analyst notes restate and normalise KPIs across banks, which is exactly what raw annual reports make hard.

source_name: OTP Bank – pénzügyi naptár (financial calendar)
why_relevant: Schedules the exact publication dates of OTP reports and Investor Day — lets the collector schedule fetches instead of polling blindly. Analogous calendars exist for MBH and Gránit.

source_name: Erste Group / Raiffeisen Bank International / Intesa Sanpaolo / UniCredit group IR — Hungary segment reporting
why_relevant: Four of the eight cell banks are foreign-owned subsidiaries. Their parents' quarterly segment reporting is often the only place Hungarian customer counts, digital-user shares and card-fee income are broken out on a quarterly cadence; the HU entity itself only files annually.

source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer (hirdetmények / eljárások)
source_subtype: national e-procurement platform / tender documentation repository
why_relevant: Mandatory national e-procurement platform: essentially all Hungarian public procurement procedures must be run in EKR. Tender documentation (műszaki leírás) for ATM operation, POS terminal supply, card personalisation and cash-logistics contracts is published here free of charge, typically containing fleet counts, transaction volumes, SLA levels and unit prices — hard quantitative data disclosed for legal reasons.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Közbeszerzési Értesítő (official procurement bulletin)
why_relevant: Official gazette of Hungarian public procurement. Below-EU-threshold and national notices — including ATM operation, cash transport, ticket-vending machine and payment-IT contracts — are published here with subject, estimated/awarded value and winning bidder. Confirmed to hold banking/cash-relevant notices (e.g. banknote-processing machine purchase, cash transport awards).

source_name: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis – hirdetménykereső (Public Procurement Database search)
why_relevant: Searchable back-end of the Hungarian procurement registry: notices and contract documents by contracting authority, CPV code (incl. obsolete codes) and free text. The most efficient single entry point for systematic CPV-driven retrieval of ATM/POS/card/cash-handling contracts across years.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ supplement), Hungary notices
why_relevant: All above-EU-threshold Hungarian contracts (large ATM outsourcing, national card-personalisation, cash-in-transit frameworks, core payment IT) must be published on TED, in structured eForms with CPV codes, estimated and awarded values, and winning economic operators. Gives cross-border comparability and the cleanest machine-readable form of the same data as Közbeszerzési Értesítő.

source_name: TED Open Data Service / data.ted.europa.eu
why_relevant: Bulk, structured open-data distribution of TED notices — enables longitudinal analysis of Hungarian ATM/POS/cash contract values, buyer concentration and vendor market shares over many years without page-by-page scraping.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Beszerzések, pályázatok (procurement page)
why_relevant: Magyar Posta is a state-owned utility-sector contracting entity and a major cash-handling actor (postal money orders, cash transport, MPT Security). Its own procurement page publishes calls (hirdetmény PDFs) for cash transport, cash processing, POS/terminal and payment-IT services with volume specifications; complements the Értesítő record.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank – Beszerzési eljárások / Közbeszerzés
why_relevant: The central bank is a contracting authority and buys banknote-processing machines, cash-cycle systems, banknote logistics and payment-infrastructure IT. Notices and archives reveal machine counts, multi-year maintenance scopes and incumbent vendors (e.g. closed-system banknote processing with 5-year maintenance seen in the Értesítő).

source_name: DKÜ Zrt. – Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség (centralised government IT procurement)
why_relevant: DKÜ centralises all government IT procurement (Korm. rendelet 301/2018). Payment-IT, card-issuing systems, terminal software and related services bought by state institutions and state-controlled companies flow through DKÜ's framework agreements — a chokepoint revealing which vendors are qualified/incumbent for state payment IT.

source_name: KEF – Központosított Közbeszerzési Portál (kozbeszerzes.gov.hu)
why_relevant: Central purchasing body for government institutions, running framework agreements and e-procurement services. Relevant as the channel through which ministries/agencies buy card-accepting equipment, ticketing/payment devices and related services; supplier lists reveal incumbents for state-sector demand.

source_name: Opentender.eu – Hungary procurement analytics (DIGIWHIST)
why_relevant: Re-processes Hungarian TED and national notices into a normalised, analysable database with buyer/supplier entities and indicators. Useful for quickly quantifying vendor market shares and contract concentration in ATM/POS/cash CPV categories without building the ETL from scratch.
